newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Japan says EU is 'main obstacle' to infotech deal.
newsitem.headline: Japan says EU is 'main obstacle' to infotech deal.

text.p: SINGAPORE, Dec 9 (REUTER) - The European Union (EU) is the "main obstacle" to concluding a deal at the World Trade Organisation (WTO) ministerial meeting to eliminate tariffs on information technology products like semiconductors, a Japanese Foreign Ministry spokesman said on Monday.
"The main obstacle is the European Union," the spokesman told reporters.

Delegates from the world trade body's 128 members, including the Big Four trade partners -- the United States, the EU, Canada and Japan -- are trying to strike an Information Technology Agreement (ITA) by the closing session of their week-long ministerial gathering on December 13.
Japan, a key player in the global infotech market whose tariffs are already at or close to zero on such products, strongly backs the U.S.-led ITA initiative.
"We are very much determined and we really wish all countries would join," the spokesman said.
But he said Tokyo was concerned at an effort by Brussels to link elimination of high-tech tariffs to non-tariff issues such as further liberalisation of government procurement.
"We believe it is important to abolish tariffs in semiconductors. Why bring in other issues -- that could be seen as just delaying tactics," the spokesman said of the EU stance.
He said, however, that Japan was "not that pessimistic" about prospects for an ITA deal this week. But he added: "We will see."

The spokesman urged the EU to make further efforts towards an agreement. "We sincerely hope the EU will make desperate efforts. It's not good to make some linkage...tariffs are tariffs. You have to tackle tariffs," he said.
